sections.heading: C — Traffic signals and pavement markings
sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic signals and pavement markings

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A55
Traffic signals regulate traffic flow, chiefly through intersections. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A55
A vertical traffic signal places red above yellow, with green at the bottom. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A55
A horizontal traffic signal places red on the far left, yellow in the middle and green on the far right. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A55
A steady circular red signal requires a complete stop before the stop line, crosswalk or intersection. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A55
A No Turn on Red notice prohibits the red-light turn discussed in the handbook's circular-red guidance. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A55
At a flashing red signal, stop completely, yield to crossing traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when clear. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A55
A steady red arrow forbids a turn in its direction until a green or yellow indication permits that movement. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A55
A yellow circular signal warns that the indication is about to become red. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A55
Before entering on a yellow circular signal, a driver should stop when a safe stop is possible. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A55
A driver already in the intersection on a circular yellow should keep moving and clear it safely. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A55
A flashing circular yellow signal calls for slowing, checking carefully for hazards and continuing cautiously. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A55
A solid yellow arrow warns that the turn signal is changing. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A55
Before entering on a solid yellow arrow, a driver should stop if it can be done safely. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A55
A driver already in the intersection on a solid yellow arrow should continue the turn and clear the intersection safely. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A56
A flashing yellow arrow permits a turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians in crosswalks. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A56
A circular green indication allows forward travel. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A56
A driver turning left from a left-turn lane on circular green must first yield to oncoming traffic and crosswalk pedestrians. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A56
Even on a signal allowing movement, a driver should not enter unless there is enough room beyond the intersection for the entire vehicle to clear it. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A56
A doghouse signal is commonly used for a protected left turn. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A56
The yellow indication on a doghouse signal means the protected left-turn movement is ending. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A56
Treat an intersection with a nonfunctioning traffic signal as a four-way stop. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A56
A pedestrian hybrid beacon has two red lenses above one yellow lens. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A56
Pedestrian hybrid beacon lights are mounted over the highway on a mast arm and along the roadside. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A57
A side street controlled by a stop sign remains stop-controlled when a pedestrian hybrid beacon is installed. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A57
Before turning a corner, watch for people who are about to cross the street. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A57
The pedestrian hybrid beacon remains dark until a pedestrian presses the crossing button. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A57
A pedestrian hybrid beacon's flashing yellow phase warns approaching drivers to slow down. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A57
The pedestrian hybrid beacon changes from flashing yellow to steady yellow to tell drivers to prepare to stop. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A57
Two steady red lights at a pedestrian hybrid beacon require a complete stop at the stop line. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A57
When a pedestrian hybrid beacon alternates flashing red lights, stop, yield to crosswalk pedestrians and proceed only when the crosswalk is clear. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A57
When the pedestrian hybrid beacon returns to darkness, drivers may proceed if the crosswalk is clear. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0057]

Misconceptions: A green indication does not authorize entry when there is no space beyond the intersection; a flashing yellow arrow still requires yielding.
Mnemonic: Color, shape and space is a teaching reminder to read the indication and confirm a clear exit.
Glossary: A circular signal differs from an arrow; a pedestrian hybrid beacon has staged pedestrian-crossing indications; a shared center lane is for turns rather than through travel.
Dynamic facts: local signal timing, closures and installed turn restrictions are not assigned invented values.

verification_debt.claim_text: The circular-red paragraph gives a generic turn permission, but the precise permitted direction and road configuration must come from the handbook's turn rules. This dossier states the no-turn-on-red prohibition without inventing blanket permission for every turn.
